title: Intra-month sliding-window burst credits for reserved capacity
creator: Priya Mehta
description:
Problem: Reserved-capacity customers occasionally need short, intra-month burst capacity that can't be accommodated by monthly quota top-ups. Current models only allow monthly resets, prorated transfers, or immediate overage charging. This causes either (a) costly overages for customers doing expected bursty jobs, or (b) manual ops interventions to temporarily increase reservations.

  Goal: Add a deterministic sliding-window credits system that allows each tenant with reserved capacity to accumulate and spend 'burst credits' within the month. Credits should be derived from unused reserved throughput, decay predictably, be conservatively capped to avoid long-term banking, and reconcile deterministically with billing and reserved pool accounting. The mechanism must be robust to retries, cross-region clock skew, and avoid false double-counting during leader failover.

  High-level approach: (1) Track per-tenant sliding-window utilization over a 7-day lookback sampled hourly, compute a conservative credit budget as a percentile of unused capacity, and emit a 'burst-credit' token granting short-term additional capacity. (2) Credits have an explicit TTL (e.g., 72 hours) and a consumption-first enforcement path in the rate limiter that prefers credits before charging overage buckets. (3) Provide admin controls in Console for cap tuning, emergency top-ups, and telemetry per tenant.

  Data model changes: Add concise ledger entries to the tenant quota store: event_type in ["credit_alloc","credit_consume","credit_expire","credit_revocation"], amount_tokens, source_window_start, window_percentile, ttl_iso. Ledger rows are append-only and idempotent by event_id to survive retries. Aggregate views compute effective available_quota = base_reserved + active_credits - consumed_active_credits.

  API/Enforcement changes: Modify token service to consult new credits table with a single read-before-write atomic check using conditional compare-and-swap on the tenant's allocation key. Enforcement logic: 1) attempt normal reservation from reserved bucket; 2) if insufficient and active credits exist, decrement credit ledger and grant tokens; 3) fallback to overage or hard-block depending on tenant policy. All transitions logged to the billing-audit stream for reconciliation.

  Migration and rollout: Start as behind-a-flag feature for 10 pilot customers. Phase 1: simulation-only mode (no enforcement, just telemetry and billing reconciliation checks) for two weeks. Phase 2: soft-enforcement for pilot tenants with max credit caps at 5% of monthly reserved capacity. Phase 3: graduated rollout with metrics and circuit-breakers (if underwriter error rate > 0.5% revert to simulation).

  Observability & metrics: New dashboard with per-tenant metrics: credit_alloc_rate, credit_consume_rate, credit_expiry_rate, delta_between_ledger_and_billing, reconciliation_discrepancies. Add tracing spans and tags for event_id and enforcement_path. Export daily reconciliation job results to BigQuery for audit and billing export.

  Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field below.
acceptance_criteria: Simulation mode runs for pilot tenants and shows expected credit allocation signal within 48h of enabling
Soft-enforcement grants burst tokens for test tenants without producing billing mismatches beyond 0.1% compared to baseline for 7 days
All credit events are idempotent and contain event_id; retrying allocation requests does not duplicate credits
Reconciliation pipeline detects ledger vs billing divergences and produces <50 mismatches/day for pilot set
Rate limiter reads credits and enforcement path latency overhead <5ms p50 and <15ms p99
Console shows per-tenant active_credits and allows admin revocation
Automatic expiry of credits after TTL and correct recording of credit_expire ledger events
migration_plan: 1) Deploy schema change for credit ledger as append-only table with event_id and tenant_id; run backfill job to compute historical sliding-window unused capacity for pilot tenants. 2) Launch simulation mode (feature flag) that writes but does not enforce credits; monitor reconciliations for 2 weeks. 3) Enable soft-enforcement for pilot tenants with tight caps; observe metrics for 7 days. 4) Widen rollout to 20% of reserved customers and increase caps if reconciliation is clean. 5) Post-rollout run a full-month billing alignment job and publish runbook for SRE/FinOps to handle disputes.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: double-allocation during leader failover. Mitigation: make allocation operation idempotent via event_id and CAS against tenant allocation key. Risk: divergence between ledger and billing export due to eventual consistency. Mitigation: daily reconciliation job and short TTL on credits so unbounded drift is impossible. Risk: credit abuse by synthetic traffic. Mitigation: apply fraud detection rules and require accounting traces on all credit consumes; use conservative percentile (e.g., 90th unused) for allocation. Risk: increased latency in hot path. Mitigation: local cache for active credits with soft-TTL and fallback to authoritative store for negative cases.
notes: Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/BR-8472-Intra-month+Burst+Credits (internal). Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4921. Reconciliation dashboard (internal Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.company/d/credits/reconciliation. Related policy doc for reserved customers: Drive/Reserved_Capacity_Policies.pdf. Billing export proto: gs://redwood-billing/exports/2025/credits-schema-v1.avsc
comments: 2025-11-10 Priya Mehta: Created ticket after call with Sales and FinOps; customers A and B requested predictable intra-month bursts, have run into manual ops escalations twice in Q3.

2025-11-12 Marco Ruiz: Reviewed data model; suggested adding event_id and making ledger append-only to simplify audit. Marked dependency on ENG-30577 (staggered quota replenishment snapshot) because we need consistent snapshots for window calculation.

2025-11-15 Sienna Chen: Prototype of windowing algorithm pushed to PR #4921. Initial allocator uses 7d hourly lookback and computes 20th percentile of unused capacity; changed to 10th percentile after load testing to be conservative.

2025-11-18 Oliver Grayson: Implemented idempotent allocation path with CAS; added metrics for allocation latency and reconciliation mismatch counter. Deployed simulation flag to staging for two pilot tenants.

2025-11-21 Aisha Patel: Observed simulation telemetry. Allocation signal stable; reconciliation mismatches ~0.04% over 48h. Noted edge-case where tenant timezones caused window alignment issues — we will align windows to tenant billing anchor rather than UTC.

2025-11-25 Priya Mehta: Product approved soft-enforcement for pilot tenants with 5% cap. Need SRE runbook draft and support channel for early revocations. Assigned follow-ups: ENG-79045 (SRE runbook) and ENG-79046 (console revocation UI).

2025-11-27 Oliver Grayson: Starting soft-enforcement rollout for tenants T-17 and T-42 behind flag. Monitoring: credit_consume_rate and delta_between_ledger_and_billing. Will escalate if reconciliation_discrepancies exceed threshold after 24h.
